wrought: shaped or made by hand; past tense of work, archaic
rebellious: defiant, refusing to obey authority or accept control
tremulous: trembling or quivering slightly, from fear or emotion
flayed: skinned or stripped of skin, often as punishment
sleek: smooth, glossy, and well cared for in appearance
scarce: hardly, barely; only just, or in very short supply
albeit: even though; although, a formal way of saying it
nought: nothing at all; zero, an archaic word for nothing
tom-toms: drums played with the hands, used in African and other music
cavalier: a dashing, careless gentleman; here, a haughty horseman
honeyed: sweet as honey; smooth, pleasant, and sugary in tone
baited: tormented or teased, as one would bait an animal
barbaric: primitive, savage, or uncivilized in behavior or nature
defiled: made dirty, impure, or morally corrupted by contact
carnal: relating to the body and its physical, sensual desires
writhes: twists the body back and forth in pain or struggle
mystic: relating to hidden spiritual truths or mysterious religious experience
pagan: heathen; not following a major organized religion
nothingness: a state of emptiness; having no existence or substance
crimson: a deep, rich red color, like dark blood
dreadful: terrible, causing great fear or distress
labored: worked with great effort; strained, heavy, or difficult
bliss: perfect happiness or joy, a state of great delight
spurned: rejected with scorn or contempt, pushed away disdainfully
crust: the hard outer layer of something, such as bread or earth
measures: rhythmic beats or musical passages, as in a song
ember: a small glowing piece of burning wood or coal
throb: a strong, rhythmic pulsing or beating, as of the heart
lyric: a short poem expressing personal feeling, often sung
timid: shy, fearful, and lacking confidence or boldness
scorn: open contempt or disdain for someone thought worthless
silken: made of silk; smooth, soft, and delicate to the touch
brute: a cruel, coarse person; or an animal lacking reason
primal: basic, original, and close to instinct or nature
bough: a large branch of a tree, usually one growing from the trunk
stoop: bend the upper body forward and downward, often in humility
trunk: the main thick stem of a tree; or the body without limbs
creep: move slowly and quietly, often with fear or stealth
marvel: a wonderful, astonishing thing that causes great admiration
subtle: slight or delicate, hard to notice or easily understood
gleam: a faint or brief shine, a soft glow of light
flung: threw forcefully or carelessly; past tense of fling
ancient: very old, dating from long ago in history
wonder: a feeling of amazement or awe at something remarkable
bitterness: resentment or sharp hurt; a harsh, sour quality
surge: a sudden powerful rush forward, as of a wave or emotion
sacrifice: giving up something valued for the sake of a greater cause
mortal: subject to death; human, as opposed to divine
clung: held tightly to something; past tense of cling
tangled: twisted and knotted together in a confused mass
pressed: pushed firmly against something, or forced down onto it
sobbed: cried with short, broken, noisy breaths of grief
conquered: defeated and taken control of by force
sensitive: easily affected by feelings, or responsive to small stimuli
naked: without clothes; bare, unprotected, or fully exposed
courage: the strength to face danger, fear, or difficulty bravely
grief: deep sorrow, especially caused by a loss or death
creed: a set of beliefs or principles, especially religious ones
lightning: a sudden flash of electric light in a storm sky
sword: a long metal weapon with a blade, used for fighting
thighs: the upper parts of the legs between hip and knee
bleed: lose blood from a wound; or feel deep emotional pain
cloud: a visible mass of water vapor floating in the sky
scenes: pictures or views of events, as in a play or painting
shade: partial darkness, or a protected area from sunlight
